answer: In an agent market selling river forecasts and opal appraisals, each identity must lock a $100 bond for 30 days before it can submit one bid per hour. Ten thousand fake agents therefore require $1 million immobilized for a month; creating more keys provides no extra bidding capacity without more bonds. Even when demand hits its nadir, the bond stays fixed, making a sybil swarm costly in capital and foregone interest.
